pageCache.text:
Where Children Can Be The Best That They Can Be
Welcome to Hillside Junior School
We are a school that promotes the 6 Rs Respect Responsibility Resourcefulness Resilience
Relationships and Reflection in our core values
Hillside Junior School is a warm and caring environment where children can reach their true potential. We believe children should take responsibility for their learning. To support them on this journey, we develop their skills to ensure they can achieve this and are prepared to succeed in the future. At Hillside Junior we have a great staff team who work together to provide a relevant and high-quality curriculum. We celebrate the diversity of our children and we are a fully inclusive school. Our wide and varied after-school activities reflect the importance we put on providing as many opportunities for our pupils. Parents and carers are welcomed into the school and we are proud of our links with the local community. As a Foundation School we work closely with our Governors to ensure that every child has a safe and happy environment in which to flourish. Visits to the school are warmly welcomed. Mr.Davies | Headteacher

British Values
The DFE have recently reinforced the need, ‘to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.’ At Hillside we believe that these are embedded in our Spiritual, Social, Moral and Citizenship education, which runs through our whole curriculum. We also promote the 6 Rs respect, responsibility, resourcefulness, resilience, relationships and reflection in our core values

Vision & Values
Mission Statement:
At Hillside Junior School, through a holistic approach, we will provide an exciting and enriched curriculum. Our school community acknowledge that physical and mental well-being are essential for children to achieve and succeed to become citizens of the future.
Vision:
Hillside children are enthusiastic and are fully engaged with our inclusive and challenging curriculum offer. Our children have a strong sense of community, belonging and show compassion for others. Our children are curious about the world and independent learners who rise to a challenge. Our children have a sense of accomplishment and pride in their environment.
Ethos:
Be the best that we can be
Values:
respect, responsibility, resourcefulness, resilience, reflection and quality relationships

pageCache.pageTitle: Hillside Junior School - Personal, Social & Health Education
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social & Health Education
In September 2020, it became statutory for schools to teach Relationships and Health Education. However, due to the pandemic, schools were given the flexibility to delay its introduction until the Summer Term 2021.
You can read about these changes in this DfE guide for parents here. The DfE strongly encourages primary schools to deliver sex education to help prepare children for their transition to secondary school.
Most schools are already delivering very effective Relationships and Sex Education lessons (RSE) and the new guidance is simply about ensuring that all children get the information they need and want.
At Hillside, we are using Coram Life Education (CLE), a leading children’s health and wellbeing charity, to support us in meeting these legal requirements. We will be using Coram Life Education’s online SCARF (Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience, Friendship) teaching resources. More information about Coram Life Education and SCARF can be found on their website: www.coramlifeeducation.org.uk
As part of the process of reviewing our RSE policy, we are have consulted with parents and carers.
We recognise that parents/carers play a vital part in their child’s RSE and we encourage you to discuss these themes with your child at home. If further advice or support is required, or if you have any questions about the programme please email our PSHE Co-ordinator, Ms Long, via the school office: [email protected]

Attendance
Pupil Attendance
It is essential for your child to have outstanding attendance throughout the school year. We know that good attendance is directly linked to good academic results throughout school. Each term we celebrate those children who have achieved 100% attendance and those pupils who have reached 100% for the entire academic year. Attending school regularly plays a vital part in successful learning.
The Department for Education (DfE) has set a target of at least 96% attendance for each child and we expect every child to achieve this.
Regular attendance is vital and is monitored and reported on according to statutory regulations.
Attendance and attainment are directly related and therefore it is essential that children should attend school every day.
If children are unwell and cannot attend school parents/carers are required to telephone the school office before 9:15am on the first day of absence. Alternatively an e-mail can be sent to the school via [email protected]

E-Safety
Internet Safety and your child
The internet has become an important part of our lives. A world has opened up which offers many positive opportunities. Children at Hillside use the Internet on a regular basis to enhance their learning and we want to ensure that pupils get the most from it, by encouraging sensible behaviour. In school we have a filtering system to prevent children accessing inappropriate sites. We also have regular ‘E’-Safety activities and assemblies to remind children of the importance of keeping themselves safe online.
Some children use Facebook, Instagram and Snapchat, which can be accessed via iPod Touch, iPad and laptops. Be warned that these sites have a minimum age of 13. On our Learning Platform ‘The Hub’ we have a safe chatroom and blogging, this is constantly monitored and can only be used by logging in.

PTA
WHAT IS HILLSIDE SCHOOLS' PARENT TEACHER ASSOCIATION?
The PTA is your association! It gives all of us in the Hillside Schools community an opportunity to get to know each other and help the school. Oh – and have some fun in the process!
We hope that by sending out regular newsletters we can keep everyone up to date with up-coming events. We’ll let you know how the PTA is helping to provide items that will enhance our children’s time at school. And, of course, there’ll be info about what you can do to get involved.
Termly meetings take place and dates are published in the school newsletter.
IN THE LAST FEW YEARS……
We’ve held Christmas and Summer fairs, recycled stacks of clothes and screened films to several year groups. We run a surprise room at Christmas for children to buy a present for a loved one, and feed the families of year 6 children at the Leavers’ BBQ. We’ve had cake sales, ice cream sales, second hand uniform sales.
As well as getting to know other parents and staff better, we generally raise around £5000-£7000 to be spent equally between Infants and Juniors.
Over the last few years the school has spent the money raised by the PTA on playground equipment, netbooks and iPads, outdoor learning areas, smart screens for the classrooms, reading books and more.

School Day
Timings of the School Day
Arrival at School
Registration and lessons start at 8.40am and school is open to receive pupils from 8.35am. No responsibility is accepted for children arriving at school before this time. A member of staff is on the playground at 8.35am and will allow children to enter the school building. Any children arriving after 8.40am should be accompanied to the school office to be signed in. Any parent who wishes to see the class teacher personally should contact the school office and an appointment to see the relevant member of staff will be made as soon as possible.
Playground
Children are not permitted to use any of the playground equipment before or after school. No ball games are allowed before or after school..
Lateness
If your child is late for school, after 8.40am, you must enter the school via the Reception/Office and register your child as late.
Timings for the School Day
8.40am - Registration and lessons start
10.30am - 10.45am - Break
12.10pm - 1.10 pm - Lunch
1.10pm - Registration and lessons start
3.20pm - School finishes
End of Day Procedures
Children finish lessons at 3:20pm and are taken onto the playground by their class teacher. The children wait with their teacher until they see the adult who is picking them up. There is also a member of the Leadership Team on duty. If they are not collected by 3:25pm, they will be taken to the school office.

School Meals
Parents have the option of providing a packed lunch for their child or a school lunch can be provided, free of charge for the academic year 2023-24, by booking in advance, please see below for further information. Crisps are discouraged in packed lunches except on Fridays and children are not expected to have chocolate bars, fizzy, fruit juice/squash or energy drinks, only water is permitted.
Although lunches are free for all pupils for the academic year 2024-25, it is important to complete a Free School Meals form (available below), in case your child is eligible for extra funding. Registering for free meals could raise extra money for the school to fund valuable support like extra tuition, additional teaching staff or after school activities. This additional money is available from central government for every child whose parent is receiving one of the benefits listed on the form.
For those children bringing a packed lunch from home we need to ensure satisfactory storage of the meal until lunchtime. The packed lunch should be in a clearly labelled lunch box/bag and not in a carrier bag!
'HCL' are the catering company that supply our school meals. HCL is an established company who offer a healthy and exciting range of meals. Please download 'Welcome Letter from HCL' for further information.
Please click on HCL's booking portal, 'School Grid': www.schoolgrid.co.uk for all ordering.
Your child will be registered by us with HCL and you will receive an email containing a 're-set password' link. This link is valid for 24 hours. You will then be able to view the menus and choose with your child/children a nutritious lunch.
The School Grid website is PC/Tablet and smartphone friendly so you can order your child/children’s meals from anywhere.
If your child has specific allergies, please inform 'HCL' as soon as possible, using the following link https://specialmenu.hcl.co.uk/
There is also a Frequently Asked Questions page for your information available at https://specialmenu.hcl.co.uk/faqs
Please download the 'School Grid Parent Leaflet' for all account and booking information.
For any further booking information or queries, please telephone School Grid direct on 01506 300 310.

Secondary Transition
Starting secondary school September 2027
If you have a child born between 1 September 2015 and 31 August 2016, you must apply for your child to start secondary school in September 2027.
Every family must apply to their home borough. This means if a family live in Hillingdon you must apply through Hilingdon Council, if you live in Hertfordshire you must apply through Hertfordshire Council, even if your child attends a junior or primary school in Hillingdon. Remember, parents/carers must apply for a place, even if:
The law does not allow us to reserve secondary school places.
